---
title: "codehover (manual)"
author: "Your Name"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(magrittr)
library(codehover)
```

The manual API gives you full control: any images, any pseudo-code. Useful
when your steps are not a single ggplot `+` chain (data wrangling, maps,
mixed outputs). For ggplot chains, prefer `ch_hover()` — see the
"codehover (automatic)" template.

# 1) Create a folder and save one image per step

```{r, warning=FALSE}
dir.create("./IMG/", showWarnings = FALSE)

g <- ggplot(cars, aes(x = speed, y = dist)) +
  geom_point()
ggsave("./IMG/1.png", g, width = 4, height = 3)

g <- g + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100))
ggsave("./IMG/2.png", g, width = 4, height = 3)

g <- g + theme_bw()
ggsave("./IMG/3.png", g, width = 4, height = 3)
```

# 2) Build the hoverable table

Pipe `ch_int()`, one `ch_row()` per step, and `ch_out()`. Inside `text`
use `<br>` for line breaks and `<tab1>` ... `<tab16>` for indentation.
The result already carries its CSS and JavaScript — just print it.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
ch_int(type = "incremental") %>%
  ch_row(text = "ggplot(cars, aes(x = speed, y = dist)) + <br> <tab1> geom_point() + </tab1>",
         img = "./IMG/1.png") %>%
  ch_row(text = "<tab1> scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) + </tab1>",
         img = "./IMG/2.png") %>%
  ch_row(text = "<tab1> theme_bw() </tab1>",
         img = "./IMG/3.png") %>%
  ch_out(img = "./IMG/3.png")
```
